title: Operate Annals libraries and corpus history
summary: Create or configure a selected library, inspect state, and explicitly submit, apply, simplify, or revert corpus changes.
use_when: Library schema, statistics, explicit reconciliation application, graph normalization, history, or reversion must be operated.
Strict reconciliation JSON should be submitted without a model run.
do_not_use_when: The task is ordinary source retention, model-assisted integration, corpus exploration, or inbox operation.
The proposed procedure edits internal rows, or assumes a stale pending reconciliation can be forced.
The task requires resetting an existing library or spool.
outcome: A deterministic library read or atomic state transition whose revision, provenance, compatibility, and recovery consequences are explicit.
effects: Initialization creates revision zero with an immutable general or decisions kind. Supported schemas 3 through 6 migrate transactionally to schema 7; migration preserves existing data in its transaction.
Applying, shaking, or reverting creates an append-only commit and advances the corpus revision when it changes state.
Direct reconciliation submission validates a projected state but does not apply it.
authority: The Annals library and canonical reducer own all corpus state, reconciliation, commit, revision, and provenance records.
No model or Nucleus job is required for deterministic library operations.
success: The selected command reports the exact library registration, instruction selection, corpus revision, reconciliation, statistics, or migration result.
Instruction selection and corpus mutations are atomic. Named creation retains a durable provisioning record so interrupted filesystem publication can resume.
A confirmed shake or revert records a new commit rather than rewriting history.
failure_and_recovery: Migration rejects unsupported old or newer schemas without partial mutation.
A pending reconciliation cannot apply after HEAD or the instruction selection diverges from its frozen basis; submit under current context rather than force it.
Revert conflicts atomically when relevant facts changed; unrelated state remains untouched.
privacy: Library files contain retained source, evidence, model-run provenance, and complete corpus history and must remain private.
does_not_authorize: Applying a pending reconciliation without explicit authorization.
Bypassing confirmation, stale-state, migration, or history checks.

consumers.statement: An authorized consuming application or operator can create a named library, select its ordinary commands, and read or replace its complete librarian instructions without model execution.
An authorized local operator or expert caller may initialize, inspect, migrate, reconcile, normalize, or revert one Annals library through deterministic product-owned commands.
This capability is not ordinary source retention, model-assisted integration, inbox operation, direct row editing, or a library reset.

preconditions.statement: The caller explicitly selects the target library and holds authority for the requested mutation; initialization requires an absent destination paths, and initialization chooses the immutable library role explicitly with general as the default.

Reconciliation application requires a valid pending result whose base and instruction revision are current, shake confirmation requires the exact preview context, and revert requires relevant facts not to have conflicted.

Library initialization requires initialized private Bazaar state and a complete cell.prompts.annals selection. The default database is ~/.local/share/bazaar/bazaar.sqlite3; callers accept an absolute CELL_BAZAAR_DATABASE override. Reads fail without creating state or using embedded fallback text.

inputs.statement: Names have 1–64 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, start with a letter, and exclude list, create, and help. Instruction set requires exactly one nonblank UTF-8 document supplied inline, from --file, or from --stdin.
Inputs select one command and library, strict reconciliation JSON with work and base revision, a pending work, or a commit revision to revert.
Arbitrary SQL, forced stale application, unsupported-schema reinterpretation, history erasure, and bypass of confirmation are not accepted.

outputs.statement: Library list reports catalog registrations and provisioning state. Library show verifies identity and reports the registration, corpus revision, and selected instruction revision; neither is a live readiness probe. Instruction set returns changed plus the selected instructions object with library_id, revision, exact content, SHA-256, and recorded_at.
The selected command reports the exact initialized or migrated library, statistics, reconciliation validation, shake plan or commit, revert commit, and resulting revision as applicable.

data_semantics.statement: Annals preserves source bytes and enforces structural and evidence invariants. Each library’s stored instructions define what concepts and parent connections mean; broader/narrower conceptual scope is the default instruction document, not a universal edge meaning.

Each library database owns immutable instruction revisions and one current selection. recorded_at describes instruction selection, not source creation or graph reinterpretation. Setting current exact bytes is unchanged; A → B → A creates successive revisions.

Initialization creates revision zero with an immutable general or decisions role. Migration assigns version-3 and version-4 libraries the general role. Application, confirmed nonempty shake, and successful revert append a commit and advance the corpus. They do not rewrite history.
Direct reconciliation submission resolves and validates a complete projected corpus state but does not apply it.
Shake removes only direct parent edges already implied by longer paths, preserving reachability but not every direct-neighbor count or hop distance.

identity_and_units.statement: The Annals-owned catalog.db maps unique names and stable library IDs to managed database, config, and spool paths. It lives under ANNALS_STATE_DIR, default macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Annals or other platforms ~/.local/share/annals. New libraries live under libraries/LIBRARY_ID/.

The selected library, its persistent ID and immutable role, public cN concept IDs, normalized work labels, reconciliation identity, commit identity, and integer corpus revision are distinct selectors.
Statistics and shake plans report documented record and edge counts rather than usage or billing units.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Instruction history returns newest-first instructions and has_more, default limit 20 and maximum 100. --before REVISION selects strictly older revisions. Instruction changes affect future examinations, start no reinterpretation, and do not advance corpus revisions.
Validation re-resolves the stored request against its exact base rather than trusting a cached projection.

Corpus and instruction mutations check their current library state at commit time and either apply their complete atomic transition or leave it unchanged. Named creation has an explicit recoverable provisioning lifecycle.
No maximum library size or migration latency is promised.

access.statement: Library inspection, instruction reads, statistics, history, and reconciliation inspection require only read access to their selected state and prepared SQLite sidecars. Query scratch storage stays in memory. Initialization and migration prepare persistent WAL files; migration also prepares the configured spool control lock. Reads never perform setup or recovery.

A registered name scopes ordinary commands as annals library NAME COMMAND. The catalog resolves and verifies stable library identity and managed paths; unknown names fail without creation. Operator config/path selection remains supported.

Named scope rejects --library, ignores ANNALS_LIBRARY, and verifies the selected persistent identity. An explicit config may tune execution but cannot redirect the registered database or spool or bypass its admission kind. Operator paths can be pinned with expected_library_id or --expected-library-id.
The supported boundary is the local Annals CLI operating one explicitly resolved private library and an explicitly chosen request file where applicable.
Direct SQLite mutation, manual database replacement, remote administration, and model execution are not supported by this capability.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Creation durably reserves one name and identity in provisioning, then publishes matching private database/config/spool state as ready. Repeating the same name and kind resumes or returns that library; conflicting state fails without replacement. Creation adds no schedule or model job.

Instruction replacement and selection are one transaction. Material application checks the stored instruction revision with HEAD. Shake confirmation also binds its instruction selection; reachability preservation does not guarantee preservation of application meaning for a direct edge.
Supported migrations and all corpus mutations are transactional; failure or conflict leaves no partial transition.

Application requires unchanged base HEAD and instruction selection, confirmed shake binds to exact library identity, HEAD, and instruction revision, and revert appends an inverse commit while preserving unrelated intervening facts.
Initialization refuse replacement, and migration rejects unsupported older or newer schemas without partial reinterpretation.

Callers resolve cell.prompts.annals to exact component versions before preparing new work. Prompt edits affect new selections. Retained requests, packet inputs, library revisions, and assignment snapshots preserve their existing recovery and retention semantics.

operational_limits.statement: Library rename, deletion, combined queries, cross-library transactions, and automatic adoption of existing operator-selected libraries are not supplied by these commands.
Migration accepts only documented prior schemas. Initialization never overwrite. Stale reconciliation has no force path. Data reset and data restore are unsupported.
No maximum library, reconciliation, or commit size, throughput, or wall-clock latency is promised here.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Required feature versions identify compatible library and corpus-change meaning. Library schema, provider release, output schema, and package generation remain separate.
No universal migration window, client support period, or deprecation interval is promised.

reliances.statement: Library initialization and prompt-selection maintenance use Bazaar immutable text. Annals owns selection JSON, rendering, domain effects, and recovery.

session_surfaces: selected local Annals library and config
Annals CLI or provider-owned typed client
Bazaar CLI for authorized prompt edits
steps: Select and verify the intended library identity, kind, prepared state, and authority for the chosen effect.
Create or resume a named library, choose exact instructions, or run authorized initialization, supported migration, statistics.
For corpus changes, prepare strict reconciliation JSON, submit and inspect it, then apply only with explicit application authority and current HEAD plus instructions.
Preview and confirm only intended shake removals, or inspect and revert an exact commit; verify the new durable commit and unrelated remaining state.
For authorized prompt edits, publish component versions before the complete Bazaar selection and verify exact pinned values.
checkpoints: The selected library ID and immutable kind match the intended target.
Initialization destination is absent; migration supports the existing schema.
The reviewed proposal or shake basis is current at atomic application.
The durable receipt, instruction revision, or corpus commit proves the selected operation outcome.
adaptation: Use registered-name or explicit operator selection without bypassing identity checks.
Repeat only the same name and kind to resume provisioning; inspect pending state before choosing a new reconciliation.
Use the installation recovery route when prepared state is unavailable rather than modifying stored records.
stop_when: Identity, admission kind, provisioning state, or supported schema cannot be established.
A reconciliation or shake basis is stale, validation fails, or a revert conflicts.
The chosen effect requires authority beyond the selected operation or storage cleanup consent.
